newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine gets U.S. funds for energy saving plan.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine gets U.S. funds for energy saving plan.

text.p: The United States has granted Ukraine funding for a feasibility study which could result in a $35 million energy savings project, U.S. officials said on Thursday.

"This is partial funding for a feasibility study of energy efficiency investments at three Ukrainian facilities," Richard Morningstar, special adviser to U.S. President Bill Clinton, told at a news conference.

The $784,500 study will be paid by a $400,000 grant from the U.S. Trade and Development Agency and $384,500 from U.S. companies Honeywell, Inc. and Armstrong International, which will conduct the study along with a Ukrainian firm.

The final project hopes to increase energy efficiency at the Kremenchug oil refinery and hydro power station in eastern Ukraine, the Kharkivenergo electrical power generation facility in the industrial city of Kharkiv and the Zhydachivsky pulp and paper plant in western Ukraine.
The agreement was signed during meetings of a special committee established by Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma and American Vice-President Al Gore.
